statements.text: Thank you, Chairman Gallagher, for your leadership on this issue and to our witnesses for helping to inform Congress on these important issues. [...] I am concerned with the rapid advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning, specifically with our adversaries like China.
statements.context: House hearing on AI in military applications where Rep. LaLota introduces transparency legislation and questions witnesses on DOD AI adoption relative to adversaries.

statements.text: Along with my colleagues from both sides of the aisle, I am concerned with the rapid advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning, specifically with our adversaries like China. What concerns me most is the Chinese Communist Party has been making great strides and intends to be the world’s leader by 2030.
statements.venue: House Armed Services Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation hearing 'Man and Machine: AI on the Battlefield'

statements.text: My legislation would require the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance to Federal agencies to implement transparency practices relating to the use of AI and machine learning, specifically when AI is being used to supplant a human’s decision making impacting American citizens.
statements.venue: House Armed Services Subcommittee hearing on AI on the battlefield

statements.text: The integration of AI and machine learning technologies with unmanned and remotely operated undersea vehicles is critical to enabling UUVs to operate independently and autonomously.
statements.context: Written question for the record submitted by Representative LaLota to Admiral Aquilino during a House Armed Services Committee hearing on U.S. military posture in the Indo-Pacific.

statements.text: Productive meeting with SUNY Chancellor John King and his team yesterday! Discussed Stony Brook and how federal investments in AI, quantum research, and workforce development can drive innovation and opportunity across Long Island. https://t.co/iKC6OdYjf6

And any AI used within the House must meet the highest standards for data security and privacy, and I appreciate your commentary earlier. And, most importantly, it must never be used in a way that undermines the trust or safety of Members, staff, or the American people.
statements.context: House Appropriations Subcommittee hearing on Legislative Branch funding for FY2026.

statements.text: You know, artificial intelligence, probably the biggest area where that is assisting us is in the screening process, where you have X-ray machines that can identify prohibited items when they come through. And that technology is improving every single day. And so we certainly stay in touch with the vendor that we use for our machines to make sure that we have the latest upgrades from that vendor. You know, it is not perfect. You are always going to need to have human eyes on those screens and human interactions with those individuals that have been identified as to having some prohibited item. But the AI helps us avoid those what we call single points of failure, where you can have one person miss something and then you could have a problem. AI can give us that backup, which is better for our security campus-wide.
statements.context: U.S. House Legislative Branch Appropriations hearing for fiscal year 2026, discussing the U.S. Capitol Police modernization plan.

statements.text: At a time where a department that is inherently research- and process-based has a new tool in AI to avail itself of, at the same time that you are able to gain those efficiencies, you are also asking for 8 percent—not 2 or 3 percent, but 8—in order to build your staff up. [...] So I guess my question then, Doctor, is: Why does the CBO need more people at a time where there is such a tool out there to make your job more efficient, sir?
statements.context: House Appropriations Subcommittee hearing on the Legislative Branch budget for Fiscal Year 2026, questioning the Congressional Budget Office Director about staffing requests.

statements.text: So I guess my question is, can you show us a report looking internally to your 270-person department that harnesses AI and to tell us that, given AI, you might need less people or you might be able to cut costs or provide more efficiencies?
statements.context: House Legislative Branch Appropriations hearing for FY2026, where a member questions an agency head about using AI to reduce staffing costs.

statements.text: Businesses across America are using AI tools like ChatGPT to cut costs and boost efficiency. Government should too. I asked the CBO Director whether taxpayers should fund more staff—or if AI can do the job more efficiently. Let’s bring gov’t into the 21st century. https://t.co/FHI8zSxBuh

As a father of three daughters, I’m proud to co-sponsor the Take It Down Act to help victims—especially minors—fight AI-generated explicit content. We must act now.

Read more: https://t.co/a2nsQ4vEke

As a father raising three daughters in an increasingly digital world, I’m alarmed by the rise of AI-generated explicit content and the exploitation of innocent people online. The TAKE IT DOWN Act is a critical step to hold bad actors accountable and ensure that social media and web platforms aren’t complicit in the spread of digitally forged, graphic images.

statements.text: Deeply concerned about AI phone scams targeting seniors. I asked @BrendanCarrFCC at a recent hearing how Congress can help @FCC crack down on this growing threat. https://t.co/sEb3X7i958
From the internet to space, medicine to AI—America's spirit of innovation drives progress and makes us the greatest nation on Earth. 🇺🇸
For 80+ years, our military has been the greatest force for good. The FY2026 NDAA invests in AI, drones, and robotics to keep us the world’s most advanced fighting force.

Before boarding my flight to D.C. this morning, I had the chance to join Hofstra University’s annual legislative breakfast. There’s real momentum on campus: a forward-looking and ethical approach to AI, expanded educational programming for Long Island’s seniors, and plans to create a dynamic on-campus “downtown.” Always a highlight to reconnect with familiar faces—especially Dean Janet Lenaghan, who was one of my MBA professors.

Spoke with @SECNAV at today’s For Country Caucus meeting about shipbuilding and how lessons from Ukraine—AI, automation, and unmanned systems—should shape our approach to deterring China in the Taiwan Strait.

As a USNA grad and former SWO, I’ll keep working with the Pentagon and with both parties to support our Troops and keep America safe.

I voted YES on the overwhelmingly bipartisan FY2026 NDAA because it delivers real results for our Service Members and our national security. The bill provides a 3.8% pay raise, invests in barracks, housing, healthcare, and mental health services, and strengthens our military’s readiness with modern ships, aircraft, missile defense, and next-generation technologies like AI and quantum. It also reforms a broken Pentagon acquisition system to get capabilities to the warfighter faster and more efficiently. This NDAA keeps America strong, supports our Troops and their families, and ensures we are prepared to deter our adversaries and win if called upon.

As DOE Undersecretary Gil noted in a recent hearing, Brookhaven National Lab’s role in launching the Protein Data Bank more than 50 years ago created a dataset that now allows AI to predict millions of protein structures—accelerating breakthroughs in medicine, chemistry, and engineering.

Smart investments in Long Island research fuel innovation, strengthen U.S. leadership, and keep us ahead of global competitors. I’ll keep fighting to ensure Long Island—and BNL—remain central to America’s research and development future.

America must win the Artificial Intelligence race and get it right.

That means embracing innovation while putting smart safeguards in place to address real risks.

At a recent Homeland Security AI Demo Day, I saw how bad actors are already using this technology to do harm. It was eye opening and concerning. 

The good news is our security professionals are adapting quickly to stay one step ahead and keep America safe.

This week in Washington, I proudly welcomed my friend, Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao, to a meeting of the bipartisan Navy and Marine Corps Caucus.

Secretary Cao came to America as a Vietnamese refugee, enlisted as a Seaman Recruit, graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy, and went on to lead Navy Diver and Explosive Ordnance Disposal teams during nearly three decades of service. Few careers better embody what it means to answer America's call.

We discussed strengthening our shipbuilding industrial base, accelerating the Navy's adoption of AI and autonomous systems, improving quality of life for our Sailors and Marines, and streamlining the defense procurement process.

As a fellow Naval Academy graduate and co-chair of the Navy and Marine Corps Caucus, I'm grateful for Secretary Cao's leadership as we work together to ensure our Navy and Marine Corps remain the strongest fighting force the world has ever known. 🇺🇸

Great meeting with Suffolk County constituent and three-time Academy Award-nominated composer Carter Burwell (Fargo, No Country for Old Men, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri). 

He joined ASCAP to discuss a simple principle, intellectual property belongs to its creator. If an AI company wants to use someone's creative work to train its models, it should ask permission, provide attribution, and pay for its use. I agree.
